text:
Alex: ALERT: p99 spike in Oslo POP (oslo-pop) since ~09:12 UTC — p99 +300ms, p50 stable. KV cache miss rate jumped 2%->18%. kernel selection logs show lots of fallbacks to generic_slow_kernel. Any recent changes?
Maria: saw it on dashboards, also a spike in cross-pop RTT to AMS. traceroute shows path now going via provider-xyz instead of direct peering. @Chen any kernel work pushed today?
Chen: checking runtime deploys... there was a small change this morning enabling 'avx_probe' path selection for a subset of models. grepping logs: `grep -n "kernel_probe_timeout" /var/log/runtime/*.log` shows repeated timeouts around 09:10-09:15. Example: `kernel_probe_timeout model=redwood-7b node=i-0abc123 delay_ms=210`.
Samir: infra note: provider-xyz reported BGP flap at 09:09 UTC for the Oslo region, packet loss on one upstream peer. Also seeing a short DNS TTL bump from 30s->5s for oslo endpoints. Could explain increased cold-starts hitting different nodes.
Alex: Ok triage options: 1) rollback avx_probe flag on oslo canary, 2) pin batching heuristic to previous 8ms window, 3) short-term routing override to prefer AMS fallback. Which is fastest?
Chen: I can rollback the probe flag on the canary now. Quick profiler before rollback shows hotspots: `kernel_probe` (35% CPU), `kv_lookup_miss_handler` (22%), `batch_coalesce` (12%). Flamegraph snapshot attached in thread (uploaded).
InfraBot: DeployBot: canary rollback started for service=runtime-oslo, deploy_id=2026-03-18-1214.
Maria: after rollback on canary, p99 dropped ~180ms on the canary nodes within 2 mins. However global KV miss remains ~12% — likely routing is still shifting traffic to cold nodes.
Samir: I'm applying a temporary route preference so edge will prefer local POP unless path latency > 120ms. Also opened ticket with provider-xyz (TKT-5891) to investigate BGP instability.
notes: Follow-up: Chen to implement async kernel probing + safer fallback, Maria to add kernel_probe_timeout alert and batching regression test, Samir to monitor provider fix and restore normal TTLs. Recommend keeping probe disabled in oslo until kernel selection change validated.
summary: Oslo POP experienced p99 latency spike caused by kernel probe timeouts combined with a provider BGP/DNS path change that increased KV cache misses and batching window. Canary rollback improved latency; network routing fix and async probe planned.
